content: 1. Perform lipid screening after achieving optimal glycemic control, and reassess lipid levels on an annual basis. 2. Target lipid profile goals as follows: LDL cholesterol should be less than 100 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol should be greater than 35 mg/dL, and triglycerides should be less than 150 mg/dL. 3. If the desired lipid goals are not achieved, modify the patient’s diet and consider initiating pharmacologic therapy if lipid levels remain elevated after six months of dietary intervention. 4. Initiate statin therapy if LDL cholesterol levels exceed 130 mg/dL and do not improve despite implementing lifestyle modifications.
